title: Calls, texts & voice notes
goal: Handle phone calls (can you hear me?, call you back, it got cut off), talk about messages, voice notes and locations, and say 'do X and then Y', 'just', 'already', 'still' and 'not yet'.
intro:
Half of your Odia will happen on the phone: calls that break up, missed calls, WhatsApp groups, voice notes and 'send me the location'. Odia phone talk mixes native verbs with English nouns: you **ଫୋନ କରିବା** 'phone', **ମେସେଜ୍ କରିବା** 'message', **ଲୋକେସନ୍ ପଠାଇବା** 'send the location'.

The grammar in this unit is what makes your sentences flow. The **-ଇ form** (ଖାଇ, ପହଞ୍ଚି, ଦେଖି) strings actions together, 'get home *and* text me', and the endings and small words for **just** (ଏଇମାତ୍ର), **already** (-ଣି), **still** (ଏବେ ବି) and **not yet** (ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ … ନାହିଁ) are what you need to answer 'have you got there yet?' a dozen times a day.

vocab.note: ମୋତେ ଫୋନ କର 'call me'. Also କଲ୍ କରିବା.
Phone calls start with ହେଲୋ, not ନମସ୍କାର, though you add ନମସ୍କାର for elders.

vocab.en: to pick up (the phone); to lift; to take (a photo)
vocab.note: ଫୋନ ଉଠାଅ! 'pick up!'; ଫଟୋ ଉଠାଇବା 'to take a photo'.
Impersonal, like 'it is heard': ତୁମ କଥା ଶୁଭୁନି 'I can't hear you' (lit. 'your words aren't audible'). Compare ଶୁଣିବା 'to listen, hear'.
ଟିକେ ଜୋରରେ କୁହ 'speak up a bit'. Opposite: ଧୀରେ 'softly, slowly'.
ନେଟୱାର୍କ ନାହିଁ 'no signal'. Also ଟାୱାର୍ ନାହିଁ (ṭawar) 'no tower', which means the same.
କଲ୍ ଆସୁଛି 'a call's coming in'; କଲରେ ଅଛି 'I'm on a call'.
ମିସ୍ କଲ୍ ଦେବା 'to give a missed call', i.e. ring once and hang up on purpose, as a free signal ('I'm downstairs', 'call me back').
ହଉ, ଫୋନ ରଖୁଛି 'OK, I'm hanging up' is the standard way to end a call. Lit. 'to put the phone down'.
ଫୋନ ସାଇଲେଣ୍ଟରେ ଥିଲା "my phone was on silent", the universal excuse.
ମେସେଜ୍ କରିବା / ମେସେଜ୍ ପଠାଇବା 'to message, text'.
ୱାଟସଆପରେ ପଠାଅ 'send it on WhatsApp'. Often just ୱାଟସଆପ୍ କରିବା 'to WhatsApp (someone)'.
ଲୋକେସନ୍ ପଠାଅ 'send the location'; ଲାଇଭ୍ ଲୋକେସନ୍ 'live location'.
ଫଟୋ ଉଠାଇବା 'to take a photo'.
ତୁମ ନମ୍ବର ଦିଅ 'give me your number'.
With a past verb: ଏଇମାତ୍ର ପହଞ୍ଚିଲି 'I've just arrived'. Also ଏବେ ଏବେ.
ସେ ଏବେ ବି ଶୋଇଛି 'he's still asleep'.
ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଆସି ନାହିଁ 'hasn't come yet'. Colloquially ଏଯାଏ (ejae).
On its own: କାମ ସାରିଲି 'I finished work'. After an -ଇ form it means 'already, completely': ଖାଇସାରିଲି 'I've finished eating'.
ରିପ୍ଲାଏ ଦେବା / ରିପ୍ଲାଏ କରିବା 'to reply'. Native: ଉତ୍ତର ଦେବା.
ଭିଡିଓ କଲ୍ କରିବା 'to video-call'.
ଗ୍ରୁପରେ 'in the group'; ପରିବାର ଗ୍ରୁପ୍ 'the family group'.

vocab.en: (of a call) to get cut off, drop
vocab.note: ଫୋନ କଟିଗଲା 'the call dropped'. Deliberately ending it is ଫୋନ କାଟିଦେବା 'to cut the call'.

vocab.en: to run out, be used up; to end
vocab.note: ବ୍ୟାଟେରୀ ସରିଯାଉଛି 'the battery's dying'; ଡାଟା ସରିଗଲା 'my data ran out'. Compare ସାରିବା 'to finish (something)'.

phrases.note: Uses the respectful verb, because you don't know who it is yet.
ଶୁଭୁନି is the colloquial form of ଶୁଭୁ ନାହିଁ.
Present continuous as a promise, like "I'm calling you back later".

phrases.en: I'll text when I get there.

grammar.title: Do X and then Y: the -ଇ form (ଖାଇ, ପହଞ୍ଚି, ଦେଖି)
grammar.body:
English joins actions with 'and (then)': 'get home and text me'. Odia puts the first action in the **-ଇ form** (the conjunctive participle, 'having done') and only the **last** verb carries tense and person:
ଘରେ **ପହଞ୍ଚି** ମେସେଜ୍ କରିବି 'I'll get home and (then) text you'.

**Forming it**: stem + **-ଇ**: ଦେଖ- → ଦେଖି, ପଢ଼- → ପଢ଼ି, ପହଞ୍ଚ- → ପହଞ୍ଚି, ଉଠା- → ଉଠାଇ, ଖା- → ଖାଇ. Irregular-looking but common: କରି (do), ଯାଇ (go), ଆସି (come), ଦେଇ (give), ନେଇ (take), ହୋଇ (become).

**Colloquial -ଇକରି**: in speech you often hear the longer form: ଖାଇକରି, ପହଞ୍ଚିକରି. It means exactly the same.

**Without doing**: ନ + -ଇ form: କାହାକୁ **ନ କହି** ଚାଲିଗଲା 'he left without telling anyone'.

You've already met it in set phrases: ଦୟାକରି 'please' (lit. 'having done kindness'), ସମସ୍ତେ ମିଶି 'all together' (lit. 'having joined'), ସିଧା ଯାଇ ବାଁକୁ ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ.

**Trap**: both actions should have the **same subject**. If someone else does the first action ('when *you* arrive, *I'll* call'), use the -ଲେ form from Unit 19: ତୁମେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ମୁଁ ଫୋନ କରିବି.

examples.en: I'll have a quick shower and come.
Take a photo and send it to the group.

examples.native: ସେ ମୋ କଥା ନ ଶୁଣି ଫୋନ ରଖିଦେଲା।
examples.roman: se mo kôtha nô suṇi phonô rôkhidela.
examples.en: He hung up without listening to me.
Call me once you get home. (intimate)
Get an auto from the station and come straight here.

grammar.title: Just, already, still, not yet
grammar.body:
**Just (now)**: **ଏଇମାତ୍ର** (or ଏବେ ଏବେ) + past: ମୁଁ ଏଇମାତ୍ର ଉଠିଲି 'I've just woken up'.

**Already**: add **-ଣି** to a past verb. It means 'already / by now' and is everywhere in speech:
ମୁଁ ଖାଇଲି**ଣି** — I've already eaten
ଆମେ / ତୁ ଖାଇଲୁ**ଣି** — we / you (intimate) have already eaten
ତୁମେ ଖାଇଲ**ଣି** — you (familiar) …
ସେ ଖାଇଲା**ଣି** — he/she …
ଆପଣ / ସେମାନେ ଖାଇଲେ**ଣି** — you (formal) / they …
As a question it means 'yet?': ପହଞ୍ଚିଲ**ଣି**? 'have you got there yet?' Add **ସାରି-** for 'already finished': ଖାଇସାରିଲିଣି 'I've already finished eating'.

**Still**: **ଏବେ ବି** 'even now' + a present or perfect: ସେ ଏବେ ବି ଅଫିସରେ ଅଛି 'he's still at the office'.

**Not yet**: **ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** (colloquially ଏଯାଏ) + the **-ଇ + ନାହିଁ** negative from Unit 16: ସେ ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ରିପ୍ଲାଏ ଦେଇ ନାହିଁ 'he hasn't replied yet'. In fast speech: ଦେଇନି, ଆସିନି, ଖାଇନି. A one-word answer to 'already?' is ନା, ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ନାହିଁ 'no, not yet'.

**Trap**: ବି alone means 'also'; only ଏବେ ବି means 'still'.

examples.native: ମୁଁ ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଟିକଟ ବୁକ୍ କରି ନାହିଁ।
examples.roman: muṃ epôrjyôntô ṭikôṭô buk kôri nahiṃ.
examples.en: I haven't booked the ticket yet.

dialogue.title: Send the location!
dialogue.setting: Sam is trying to find Lipsa's new flat in Patia, Bhubaneswar, for her housewarming. He calls her from the main road.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ହେଲୋ? ସାମ୍? ତୁମ କଥା ଠିକ୍ ଶୁଭୁନି…
lines.roman: helo? Sam? tumô kôtha ṭhik subhuni…
lines.en: Hello? Sam? I can't really hear you…

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୁଁ ପାଟିଆ ଛକରେ ଅଛି। ତୁମ ଘର କେଉଁଠି?
lines.roman: muṃ Paṭia chhôkôre ôchhi. tumô ghôrô keuṃṭhi?
lines.en: I'm at Patia junction. Where's your place?

lines.speaker: Lipsa

lines.roman: kôṇô? ṭike jorôre kuhô! eṭhi neṭwark khôrapô.
lines.en: What? Speak up a bit! The signal's bad here.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ପାଟିଆ… ଛକ… ହେଲୋ? ଆରେ, ଫୋନ କଟିଗଲା।
lines.roman: Paṭia… chhôkô… helo? are, phonô kôṭigôla.
lines.en: Patia… junction… hello? Oh no, it cut off.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ସରି, ମୁଁ ବାରଣ୍ଡାକୁ ଆସିଲି। ଏବେ ଶୁଭୁଛି?
lines.roman: sôri, muṃ barôṇḍaku asili. ebe subhuchhi?
lines.en: Sorry, I've come out onto the balcony. Can you hear me now?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଁ, ଏବେ ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି। ମୁଁ ଅଧ ଘଣ୍ଟା ହେଲା ବୁଲୁଛି!
lines.roman: hôṃ, ebe ṭhik ôchhi. muṃ ôdhô ghôṇṭa hela buluchhi!
lines.en: Yes, it's fine now. I've been going round in circles for half an hour!

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ଅଧ ଘଣ୍ଟା? ମୁଁ ତ ଲୋକେସନ୍ ପଠାଇଦେଇଥିଲି!
lines.roman: ôdhô ghôṇṭa? muṃ tô lokesôn pôṭhaideithili!
lines.en: Half an hour? But I sent you the location!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: କେବେ? ମୋ ୱାଟସଆପରେ ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ କିଛି ଆସିନି।
lines.roman: kebe? mo waṭsapôre epôrjyôntô kichhi asini.
lines.en: When? Nothing's come through on my WhatsApp yet.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ରୁହ, ଦେଖୁଛି… ଓହୋ! ମୁଁ ଭୁଲରେ ଅଫିସ୍ ଗ୍ରୁପରେ ପଠାଇଦେଲି!
lines.roman: ruhô, dekhuchhi… oho! muṃ bhulôre ôphis grupôre pôṭhaideli!
lines.en: Hang on, let me look… oh no! I sent it to the office group by mistake!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହା ହା! ବୋଧହୁଏ ଆଜି ତୁମ ମାଲିକ ବି ଆସିବେ।
lines.roman: ha ha! bodhôhue aji tumô malikô bi asibe.
lines.en: Ha ha! Maybe your boss will turn up too today.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ଚୁପ୍! ଏଇମାତ୍ର ତୁମକୁ ପଠାଇଲି। ଦେଖି ସିଧା ଚାଲିଆସ, ମୁଁ ତଳେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରୁଛି।

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଉ, ପାଇଗଲି। ପାଞ୍ଚ ମିନିଟରେ ପହଞ୍ଚୁଛି। ମୋ ବ୍ୟାଟେରୀ ବି ସରିଯାଉଛି!
lines.roman: hôu, paigôli. pañchô miniṭôre pôhôñchuchhi. mo byaṭeri bi sôrijauchhi!
lines.en: OK, got it. I'll be there in five minutes. My battery's dying too!

culture:
Phone etiquette in Odisha is relaxed. People answer with ହେଲୋ and, if they don't recognise the number, ହେଲୋ, କିଏ କହୁଛନ୍ତି?; with elders add ନମସ୍କାର or ଆଜ୍ଞା. Calls end quickly with ହଉ, ଫୋନ ରଖୁଛି 'OK, hanging up' or ହଉ, ପରେ କଥା ହେବା 'talk later'; there's no long goodbye. Calling is still often preferred to texting, especially by older relatives, and a **missed call** on purpose is a normal signal ('I'm downstairs', 'call me back').

WhatsApp is how everything is organised, from the college gang to the extended-family group where an uncle posts *Good morning* flowers and Jagannath images every day. Voice notes are hugely popular, partly because typing Odia script on a phone is slow: many young people type Odia in Roman letters ('kana karuchu?' for କ'ଣ କରୁଛୁ?) or just send a voice note. Sending a location pin is the normal way to give directions to your home, since addresses tend to be landmark-based ('behind the temple, near the water tank'). And whenever Odias don't pick up, the phone was ସାଇଲେଣ୍ଟରେ.

tip.title: On the phone
tip.body:
- Start with **ହେଲୋ**; if you don't know who it is: **କିଏ କହୁଛନ୍ତି?**
- 'Hear' on the phone is impersonal **ଶୁଭିବା**: ମୋ କଥା **ଶୁଭୁଛି**? 'can you hear me?', **ଶୁଭୁନି** 'can't hear'.
- ଶୁଣିବା is 'to listen': don't mix them up.

sentences.en: Hello, it's Sam.
Hello, can you hear me now?
Yes, I can hear you fine now.
No, I can't hear a thing, the signal's bad.

sentences.native: ଟିକେ ଜୋରରେ କୁହନ୍ତୁ, ଏଠି ବହୁତ ଭିଡ଼।

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଫୋନ ଉଠାଇଲି, କିନ୍ତୁ କେହି କିଛି କହିଲେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ phonô uṭhaili, kintu kehi kichhi kôhile nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I picked up, but nobody said anything.

sentences.native: ଘର ଭିତରେ ନେଟୱାର୍କ ନାହିଁ, ମୁଁ ବାହାରକୁ ଆସୁଛି।
sentences.roman: ghôrô bhitôre neṭwark nahiṃ, muṃ baharôku asuchhi.
sentences.en: There's no signal indoors, I'm coming outside.
Who's speaking, please?
Dad isn't picking up.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ମିଟିଂରେ ଅଛି, ପରେ ଫୋନ କରୁଛି।
sentences.roman: muṃ miṭiṅre ôchhi, pôre phonô kôruchhi.
sentences.en: I'm in a meeting, I'll call you back.

sentences.native: ତୋର ତିନିଟା ମିସ୍ କଲ୍ ଦେଖିଲି, କ'ଣ ହେଲା?

sentences.en: I saw three missed calls from you, what happened?
Sorry, my phone was on silent.

sentences.roman: phonô uṭhailô nahiṃ kahiṃki? muṃ chinta kôruthili.
sentences.en: Why didn't you pick up? I was worried.

sentences.native: ତଳେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଗୋଟିଏ ମିସ୍ କଲ୍ ଦେ।

sentences.en: Give me a missed call when you're downstairs.

sentences.native: ହଉ, ଫୋନ ରଖୁଛି, ପରେ କଥା ହେବା।

sentences.en: OK, I'm hanging up, talk later.

I'll call you tonight.
Two minutes, I've got another call coming in.

tip.title: The -ଇ form: do X and then Y
tip.body:
- First action in the **-ଇ form**, last action with the real ending: ଘରେ **ପହଞ୍ଚି** ମେସେଜ୍ କରିବି.
- ଦେଖି, ପଢ଼ି, ଉଠାଇ, ଖାଇ, କରି, ଯାଇ, ଆସି, ଦେଇ, ନେଇ. Colloquial: ଖାଇ**କରି**.
- 'Without doing': **ନ** + -ଇ form: ନ କହି.

sentences.en: I'll text you when I get home.
I'll follow the location and come.
Take a photo of the food and send it on WhatsApp.
Write my number down.
I'll call after I've eaten.
I'll drop you a message, don't worry.

sentences.native: ସେ ମେସେଜ୍ ପଢ଼ି କିଛି ଉତ୍ତର ଦେଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: se mesej pôṛhi kichhi uttôrô dela nahiṃ.
sentences.en: He read the message and didn't answer at all.

sentences.native: ଲୋକେସନ୍ ପଠାଅ, ମୁଁ ଅଟୋ ନେଇ ଆସୁଛି।
sentences.roman: lokesôn pôṭhaô, muṃ ôṭo nei asuchhi.
sentences.en: Send the location, I'll grab an auto and come.
He left without telling anyone.

tip.title: Just, already, still, not yet
tip.body:
- **Just**: ଏଇମାତ୍ର + past: ଏଇମାତ୍ର ପହଞ୍ଚିଲି.
- **Already / yet?**: past + **-ଣି**: ଖାଇଲି**ଣି**, ଖାଇଲ**ଣି**?, ଗଲା**ଣି**, ଗଲେ**ଣି**.
- **Still**: **ଏବେ ବି**.
- **Not yet**: **ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** + -ଇ + ନାହିଁ: ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଆସି ନାହିଁ.

sentences.en: I've just got home.
He hasn't replied yet.
Have you eaten yet?
Yes, I've already eaten.

sentences.native: ସେ ଏବେ ବି ଅନଲାଇନ୍ ଅଛି, ହେଲେ ରିପ୍ଲାଏ ଦେଉନି।
sentences.roman: se ebe bi ônlain ôchhi, hele riplae deuni.
sentences.en: He's still online, but he's not replying.
My brother's still asleep.
Have you got there yet?
I'll call when I've finished work.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ତାର ମେସେଜ୍ ପଢ଼ି ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ epôrjyôntô tarô mesej pôṛhi nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I haven't read his message yet.
They've already left.

lessons.title: Voice notes, video calls and dying batteries

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଗାଡ଼ି ଚଲାଉଛି, ଭଏସ୍ ମେସେଜ୍ ପଠାଉଛି।
sentences.roman: muṃ gaṛi chôlauchhi, bhôes mesej pôṭhauchhi.
sentences.en: I'm driving, I'll send a voice note.

sentences.native: ତୋ ଭଏସ୍ ମେସେଜ୍ ଶୁଭୁନି, ପୁଣି ପଠା।
sentences.roman: to bhôes mesej subhuni, puṇi pôṭha.
sentences.en: I can't hear your voice note, send it again.

sentences.native: ରବିବାର ମୁଁ ବୋଉଙ୍କ ସହ ଭିଡିଓ କଲ୍ କରେ।
sentences.roman: rôbibarô muṃ bouṅkô sôhô bhiḍio kôl kôre.
sentences.en: I video-call Mum on Sundays.
Argh, the call dropped again!
My battery's dying, say it quick.

sentences.native: ପରିବାର ଗ୍ରୁପରେ ଜେଜେମା ସବୁଦିନ ସକାଳେ ଫଟୋ ପଠାନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: pôribarô grupôre jejema sôbudinô sôkaḷe phôṭo pôṭhanti.
sentences.en: In the family group, Grandma sends photos every morning.

sentences.native: ଗ୍ରୁପରେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ପଚାରି ପ୍ଲାନ୍ ଠିକ୍ କରିବା।
sentences.roman: grupôre sômôstôṅku pôchari plan ṭhik kôriba.
sentences.en: Let's ask everyone in the group and then fix the plan.

sentences.native: ବ୍ୟାଟେରୀ ସରିଗଲା ବୋଲି ଫୋନ ବନ୍ଦ ହୋଇଗଲା।
sentences.roman: byaṭeri sôrigôla boli phonô bôndô hoigôla.
sentences.en: My phone died because the battery ran out.

sentences.native: ନେଟୱାର୍କ ଭଲ ନାହିଁ, ଭିଡିଓ କଲ୍ ପୁଣି ପୁଣି କଟିଯାଉଛି।
sentences.roman: neṭwark bhôlô nahiṃ, bhiḍio kôl puṇi puṇi kôṭijauchhi.
sentences.en: The signal is bad, the video call keeps dropping.
